claims.text: LoggingNotifier.Send calls logger.LogInformation("notification for order {OrderId}: {Subject}", orderId, subject) - one message template, two named placeholders, two arguments.

RequestLoggingMiddleware.InvokeAsync calls logger.LogInformation with template "{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms" and four arguments: context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path, context.Response.StatusCode, stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds.

Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: a message template's {Name} placeholders become named properties on the resulting log event, distinct from the formatted message string; ILogger implementations that support structured data (not just console text) can read those properties directly.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs, Logging in .NET, "Log message template" section (learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/logging)

claims.text: C# string interpolation ($"...") is evaluated into a single string value at the point it's written, before that value is passed to any method call; a method receiving an interpolated string argument never sees the original placeholder names or the pre-interpolation values separately.
